Jokes aside (though he probably meant it 😂), I'm excited for the future. Humanity needs more Jensens in leadership positions, not less. Most of our leaders suck. Jensen is one of the good ones. Protect the good ones.

Also, I agree with Elon: stand up for people when they are down. We don't do enough of that for each other. We're human, we're flawed, but there is a lot more good in people than bad. We need to celebrate the good more.

Also, in terms of China, they should be a competitor not an enemy. The latter is the goal of warmongers. War destroys, competition creates.

My previous post last week was about Jensen's character. But even if we forget all that. Selfishly, as an American, I want America to win. And Jensen is essential to us winning, in the space of friendly competition, not military conflict and escalation.

Beware of the military industrial complex fueling hate of China. Warmongers want to create enemies, to fuel hate, division, fear. Warmongers want war, because it makes more money than anything else, they don't give a shit about the suffering it creates, or the cost it has for everyday people. Beware of the warmongers. Celebrate peacemakers. Jensen is a peacemaker.

Alright, just felt like writing this, while sitting at a gas station in the middle of nowhere. Hyped up on coffee.

I took a bit of a break, and now am back on the motorcycle. And just have to say, holy fuck is the feeling of freedom unlike anything else. Plus I had a very nice older lady a few minutes ago say I look sexy on the bike. And now I'm the meme of the guy who remembers a compliment for months/years.

I know my mom will surely kill me when she reads this. So, mom, please don't worry, everything will be great 🙏❤️

Btw, I still need to publish videos on my trip through China, where I hitchhiked about 3,000km across rural China, also interviewed some of the top AI & robotics folks there. I'll do that soon.

I'm just slow with the editing thing & bad at the filming thing. I'll try to get better. Mostly, when I travel, I focus on taking it all in and being present with the people in front of me, learning from them, while allocating no thought to the camera. The camera is a side thing I bring along sometimes because it's nice to relive those moments & to share with others.

Anyway, I'll probably take breaks from the road on occassion (to do podcasts, etc). But the goal is to eventually crisscross the country. Who knows how far I'll actually get.

And to friends who will surely write me "wtf are you doing you idiot", please don't worry, while it's true that I'm kind of an idiot, I will also make sure to be safe. Exploring the country on a motorcycle is unlike anything else, it's freedom. It makes me love this country even more: its beautiful nature and all the variety of characters who make up America. And of course, I'm trying to stay off of the interstate, taking as many backroads as I can.

I'll post video if/when I get to it. Sorry to be slow.

It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.","link":"https://x.com/lexfridman/status/2120986129671631239","description":"NVIDIA letting Jensen go is a huge mistake, for America and for humanity. It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.

I've been keeping quiet on this out of respect for Jensen's family and team, who I've met and who are amazing humans, and because I personally hate infidelity. So my heart goes out to them in this difficult personal family moment.

But I can also say that Jensen is human, and makes mistakes like all of us do. Not that I matter at all, but I've known Jensen for a long time and have gotten the chance to spend a lot of time with him, behind the scenes, away from mics and cameras. I have seen him show kindness, humility, care to everyone around him, including strangers, including from the poorest most struggling parts of society, treating all the same with the same thoughtfulness and attention, because they are fellow humans and not because he has something to gain from them. That shows rare character, to maintain humility and humanity through all of it.

Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. Probably over a thousand people at this point. This includes hundreds of engineers, CEOs, colleagues, friends, etc.

Also, since there was some spy talk. Jensen is as proud  an American as it gets. I'm in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America.

I stand with Jensen.

Humans are amazing. In part, because our minds are such a damn complicated mess.
